answer: To raise the cost of fake swarms, route every settled job through a handful of capacity-limited lanes, the way cargo must cross one public jetty. Each accepted delivery is marked with a unique pigment drawn from that agent's first paid output, then checked later against a public record as hard to rewrite as basalt. Accounts that reuse the same mark, the same funding pulse, or the same intake slot are folded into one seat and their combined influence is capped. Signing up can stay cheap; scarce lanes and consistent marks make mass influence expensive.
